speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe how the painful ulcer on your leg started and how long it has been there? Also, do you have any history of diabetes, vascular disease, or recent trauma to that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease, this could be pyoderma gangrenosum, but I need to rule out infection or vascular causes. Do you have any fever, chills, or systemic symptoms, and is the ulcer's border raised and purple?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of an ant bite followed by a rapidly expanding ulcer with purplish borders strongly suggests pathergy, a hallmark of pyoderma gangrenosum, especially given your Crohn's disease. I need to confirm the clinical appearance and rule out other causes, so please allow me to examine the lesion. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: ["Crohn's disease", 'Type 2 diabetes mellitus', 'Hypertension', 'Treated for anterior uveitis 8 months ago'] Social history: Recently returned from a visit to Wisconsin 2 months ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the image. Given your recent trip to Wisconsin, I need to rule out Lyme disease, so do you recall seeing a tick bite or having a rash resembling a bullseye before the ulcer developed? Also, have you had any joint pain or swelling in your knees or ankles?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the strong clinical picture of pathergy following an ant bite and your history of Crohn's disease, this is highly suggestive of Pyoderma Gangrenosum. I will request a skin biopsy to confirm the diagnosis and rule out infection. REQUEST TEST: Skin Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin Biopsy Histopathology shows neutrophilic infiltration without infection, consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum.
